questions.q: What does RoPE (Rotary Position Embedding) do?
options: Adds a learned position vector to each token embedding
Encodes token position by rotating attention query and key vectors
Removes the need for an attention mechanism entirely
Compresses the vocabulary to reduce embedding size
questions.explain: RoPE encodes positional information by rotating query and key vectors in attention, rather than adding a separate learned or sinusoidal position embedding.

questions.q: In a model's config.json, if num_key_value_heads equals 1 while num_attention_heads is 32, what attention variant is being used?
options: Standard multi-head attention (MHA)
Multi-query attention (MQA), where all query heads share one key/value head
Grouped-query attention (GQA) with 8 groups
No attention mechanism at all
questions.explain: When num_key_value_heads is 1, every query head shares a single key/value head -- that's multi-query attention. Equal values indicate standard MHA; an intermediate value indicates GQA.

questions.q: What is the defining difference between a dense transformer and a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model?
options: MoE models use a smaller vocabulary than dense models
Dense models activate every parameter for every token; MoE models route each token to only a subset of expert sub-networks
MoE models cannot use attention mechanisms
Dense models always have fewer total parameters than MoE models
questions.explain: A dense model computes all of its parameters for every token. An MoE model uses a router to activate only a handful of expert feed-forward networks per token, increasing total capacity without proportionally increasing per-token compute.

questions.q: What problem does grouped-query attention (GQA) primarily address compared to standard multi-head attention?
options: It eliminates the need for positional encoding
It reduces the size of the KV cache needed at inference time, at a small quality cost
It increases the vocabulary size supported by the model
It removes the feed-forward layers from the transformer block
questions.explain: GQA groups multiple query heads onto shared key/value heads, shrinking the KV cache memory footprint at inference time compared to full multi-head attention, with a modest quality trade-off.

questions.q: What is the main engineering cost introduced by a Mixture-of-Experts architecture?
options: It requires a completely different tokenizer
Routing introduces load-balancing challenges and added communication overhead in distributed training
It makes RoPE impossible to use
It eliminates the need for a compute budget
questions.explain: MoE's router must balance load across experts and, in distributed training, may need to send tokens across devices to reach the right expert -- adding real systems complexity even as it increases model capacity per FLOP.
